# Acu361

> {{TITLE}}. Acu361 gives a precise location for each of the 361 WHO standard acupoints (670 points). Every location is the consensus of a panel of seven acupuncturists, who went through the points one by one, and is recorded as a millimetre coordinate on the skin of an open anatomical body with seven layers. With surface lines of the 14 meridians, the 27 WHO proportional bone measurements in B-cun, and the body itself in seven anatomical layers. Data CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT. Version {{VERSION}}.

- Website and 3D explorer: {{SITE_URL}}
- Repository (all files, schemas, validator): {{REPO_URL}}
- Authors: Yuyue Zhang (corresponding, {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}), Timothy G Reese, Yang He, Michael Zhu; Human Motion & Molecular Health Lab, Department of Statistics, Purdue University ({{LAB_URL}})
- A point can be linked directly: {{SITE_URL}}#LU7_L opens the explorer at Lieque (LU7), left side.

## Data files

- [points.json]({{SITE_URL}}data/points.json): 670 points (309 bilateral codes x 2 + 52 midline codes). The header holds the frame, counts and field descriptions; `points` is a list of records.
- [points.csv]({{SITE_URL}}data/points.csv): the same table as CSV; columns id, code, side, meridian, index, name_pinyin, name_zh, x_mm, y_mm, z_mm, nearest_bone, bone_distance_mm.
- [meridians.json]({{SITE_URL}}data/meridians.json): surface lines of the 14 meridians on the skin, 66 segments, 10,894 samples about every 4 mm, offset 1.2 mm outward from the skin. Body-surface course only.
- [rulers.json]({{SITE_URL}}data/rulers.json): 27 proportional bone (skeletal) measurements in B-cun, 31 instances on the body (each with ends a, b in mm and the straight length), 19 derived landmarks.
- [manifest.json]({{SITE_URL}}data/manifest.json): counts, frame, size and SHA-256 of every file.
- Body: {{REPO_URL}}/tree/main/data/body holds skin, muscle, bone, ligament, organ, vessel, nerve as glTF 2.0 binary (.glb), 2,812 objects named with Z-Anatomy object names, no materials.

## Fields of a point

- id: unique point id, `<code>_<side>`, e.g. `LU7_L`
- code: WHO 2008 point code, e.g. `LU7`
- side: `L` body left, `R` body right, `M` midline (GV and CV points)
- meridian: one of LU LI ST SP HT SI BL KI PC TE GB LR GV CV
- index: number of the point within its meridian
- name_pinyin: Hanyu Pinyin without tone marks, e.g. `Lieque`
- name_zh: simplified Chinese name, e.g. `列缺`
- pos: [x, y, z] in mm on the skin surface of data/body/skin.glb
- nearest_bone: name of the bone object (in bone.glb) whose surface is closest to pos
- bone_distance_mm: straight-line distance from pos to that bone surface, 0.1 mm; a geometric distance in this model, not a needling depth

Example: {"id": "LU7_L", "code": "LU7", "side": "L", "meridian": "LU", "index": 7, "name_pinyin": "Lieque", "name_zh": "列缺", "pos": [{{LU7_POS}}], "nearest_bone": "{{LU7_BONE}}", "bone_distance_mm": {{LU7_DIST}}}

## Coordinate frame

Millimetres. +x toward the body's left, +y up, +z anterior (the body faces +z); right-handed, the glTF convention. x = 0 is the mid-sagittal plane; the soles are at y = 0; skin height 1709.5 mm. All JSON and GLB files share this frame.

## How the data were made

Each of the 361 acupoints was located by a panel of seven acupuncturists. The panel went through the points one by one. For every point, the members compared where they would place it, discussed the differences, and agreed on a single position. That agreed position was marked on the skin surface of the model in a 3D annotation tool built for this project, and it is the coordinate published here. No point rests on one person's judgment. The members of the panel are not named. Bilateral points are left-right symmetric: each right-side point is the mirror image (x -> -x) of its left-side counterpart. Point codes, the set of points, their order and the meridian names follow WHO 2008; no text of the standard is included.

## Limitations

- One body: a single adult male model in standing posture.
- bone_distance_mm is a geometric distance in the model, not a needling depth.
- Meridian lines show the body-surface course only.
- Not medical advice; for research and teaching.
